issues.description: The UML in the problem statement specifies an Animal constructor with two parameters (Animal(String, int)), but both the template usage (Main.java) and the solution implement/expect a single-argument constructor Animal(String). This mismatch between the stated constructor signature and the code will confuse students about which constructor to implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the constructor requirement consistent: either update the UML/problem statement to require Animal(String) (matching the template usage and solution), or modify the template and solution to implement Animal(String, int) and update all subclasses and example code accordingly so students clearly know which constructor signature to implement.

issues.description: The UML in the problem statement declares an 'age: int' attribute for Animal, but the provided solution (and the template usage) do not include an age attribute. This discrepancy between the UML and the codebase can mislead students about required attributes to initialize and accessors to implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Resolve the attribute mismatch by aligning the specification and code: either remove the 'age' attribute from the UML/problem statement (if age is not intended) or add an 'age' field and corresponding constructor parameter, getter, and setter to Animal and update all subclass constructors and example usages to include and initialize age.
